CURRENT USER MESSAGE: Why can a phone show its GPS position without mobile data, yet fail to show a detailed map?
ASSISTANT:

memory.scope: Sampled process peaks, not continuous maxima; includes profiling overhead. Fault counters are not physical-read counts.

answers.text: A phone can show its GPS position without mobile data because GPS relies on satellite signals to determine location. However, it may fail to show a detailed map when there is no signal from GPS satellites—such as in areas with poor coverage, dense urban environments, or during satellite outages—resulting in only a basic location pin or no map at all. Detailed maps require additional data sources, such as cellular network information or Wi-Fi signals, which are not available in GPS-only mode. [1]
